lane_crowding.label: Lane crowding
lane_crowding.reason: Each extra candidate in a pool trims everyone in it a little; at 0.15 a third candidate cost 23 percent, more than anything in the data supports, and 0.05 costs about 9.

transfer_share.label: Secondary pool transfer share
transfer_share.reason: When a candidate drops out, rivals whose second home is the same pool count half as much as rivals whose first home is.

field_leak.label: Field leak
field_leak.reason: Not every voter follows a departing candidate to a pool mate, so 30 percent of the transfer goes to the whole field in proportion to strength.

coordination.label: Establishment coordination
coordination.reason: Even odds that the strongest establishment pool consolidates behind its delegate leader after the early states, raised when Trump is strong.

coordination_failure.label: Coordination failure
coordination_failure.reason: About one run in three the establishment never consolidates, nobody steps aside, and candidates hang on to a lower vote share.

delegate_lean.label: Automatic delegate lean
delegate_lean.reason: Automatic delegates are party insiders, so 60 percent of their votes from the second ballot go to Party Anchor and Suburb candidates still standing.

debate_skill.label: Debate skill
debate_skill.reason: Half of the debating edge or weakness of each of the top four finishers carries into their strength after every contest.

random_branch_rate.label: Random branch-point events
random_branch_rate.reason: Four runs in ten get one surprise event before the field forms; this is today's rate, and the clock lowers it to a quarter by South Carolina.

dropout_transfer.label: Dropout support transfer
dropout_transfer.reason: About a third of a departing candidate's strength moves on to the candidates still running; the rest of their voters scatter or stay home.

nameid_growth.label: Name ID growth rate
nameid_growth.reason: Fitted to Pete Buttigieg going from 15 percent name ID in January 2019 to 80 percent at the Iowa caucus on his 2019 news volume (node scripts/fit_nameid.js gives 0.0474).

nameid_fav_weight.label: Favorability weight
nameid_fav_weight.reason: Net favorable among Democrats moves strength by half its size, so a candidate at plus 50 runs 25 percent stronger than one at zero.

nameid_fallback_base.label: Estimated name ID floor
nameid_fallback_base.reason: A candidate YouGov has never asked about starts as if 15 percent of voters knew them, about where a statewide officeholder with no national profile sits.

nameid_fallback_slope.label: Estimated name ID per attention point
nameid_fallback_slope.reason: Each point on the 10-point attention score adds 5 points of estimated name ID to a candidate with no YouGov reading.

nameid_fallback_cap.label: Estimated name ID ceiling
nameid_fallback_cap.reason: No estimate goes above 60 percent; a candidate known that widely would show up in a YouGov wave.
